title: Trump wasn't 'a believer' in UFOs — until Air Force saw mysterious round object
excerpt: Donald Trump said pilots told him a round UFO passed an F-22 jet at three times its speed, pledging to investigate secret government programs.
content:
See more of our coverage in your search results.

President Donald Trump said Air Force pilots told him a mysterious round object flew past an F-22 fighter jet at three times its speed, while pledging to investigate claims that a secret government program studying UFOs could exist without the president’s knowledge.

Trump made the comments during an interview with correspondent Ross Douthat that aired Sunday on CBS’ “60 Minutes.”

Douthat asked Trump whether anything the president had seen, heard or been told led him to believe there was more behind unidentified objects spotted in the sky. Trump described himself as “not too much of a believer,” but pointed to conversations with Air Force pilots in the Oval Office.

“These are not people that you would say are conspiracy theorists – they don’t even know what it means – but they’re great, great pilots,” Trump said, before joking about their appearance. “Young, handsome, they have beautiful, nice flat tops. I’d like to have a haircut just like them. They look perfect, like Tom Cruise.”

Trump called the pilots “the real deal” and said they had told him “things that are very strange.”

He described one of those encounters involving an F-22.

“They’re flying an F-22, which is the best there is, the fastest, the best plane that anyone’s ever seen,” Trump said. “And something goes by them at three times their speed. And it’s round. It’s not aerodynamic.”

Trump did not identify the pilots or say when or where the encounter occurred.

Douthat then asked Trump about claims from alleged whistleblowers that the government operates a secret program studying UFOs that even presidents may not know about.

“No, and I haven’t heard that,” Trump said. “But if there is, I’m going to find out about it right after this interview.”

Trump later said there are “a lot of very solid people” who believe such claims are true, though he remained skeptical himself.

Fox News Digital reached out to the White House for comment.

Trump’s remarks come just weeks after the Pentagon’s All-domain Anomaly Resolution Office (AARO) released a batch of recently declassified records detailing UFO sightings spanning decades.

Among them was a 2026 account from federal law enforcement agents who reported seeing a matte-black triangular object rise vertically above a mountain ridge, hover silently and then accelerate into a canyon at a speed they compared to a fighter jet.

The witnesses described no visible engines, rotors, exhaust or other conventional means of propulsion. Handheld thermal equipment also showed a uniform heat signature across the object’s surface rather than concentrated heat typically associated with a propulsion system.

The object was never identified, and the Pentagon report noted that its speed was estimated by witnesses rather than measured by instruments.
